items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: some of that neoclassical — they call it neoclassical shred is, they are Bach chord progressions and stuff.

ctx.x: Did you have a period where you were playing some fairly technical music in that genre but you had yet to find out — I hesitate to say this because it sounds like an insult almost, but you didn’t know what you were doing from a musical standpoint from a chordal standpoint, music theory? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

I think so. I mean I think that’s in everyone’s development for sure. Coming from a family of keyboard players, and I mean I mean harmony was so present in my imagination and musical world so I think that was the draw. I mean some of that actually, some of that neoclassical — they call it neoclassical shred is, they are Bach chord progressions and stuff. But did I know what it was? But that was what drew me to study at Berklee as a kid because I grew up with harmony and then you know that of course was an easy…

I’m always fascinated by — guitar players especially who are self-taught, didn’t go to music school. For about six years I played in a group that was playing early Yes and Genesis and very complex music. And the guitar players had an easier time learning it than I did. And I had graduated from music school. And their ability to hear and not get hung up about odd measures or forms was positive for them.
